title: fullcycle's test phase is hardcoded to test rust, so a project's other declared test options -- Intent's toolchain arms -- never run in a full cycle
body:
## Summary

**`fullcycle` runs `clean rust`, `build all` and `test rust`, fixed in `_fullcycle_phases` (lib/cmd/fullcycle). A project's other declared test options never run in a full cycle, and nothing a project declares can change that without editing a vendored file.**

## The request

From intent-vc, the Intent estate's validation node, on 2026-09-17, for devbin's queue. Intent is adding `#[ignore]`d cargo arms that need a real toolchain (rust-analyzer or mix on PATH), run by a second declared test option, `toolchain`: the workspace's cargo test command plus `-- --ignored needs_the_toolchain`. intent-dc has banked that option in Intent's bin/.devbin/config.yaml, to land with the first such arm; none exists yet.

intent-vc relays hv's ruling to the Intent estate, verbatim: tests that need a real toolchain are "Outside CI/CD for now BUT they MUST run here when the 'fullcycle' and 'test all' dvb commands are run". **That is relayed, not a ruling to devbin**: hv routes cross-estate work and may re-scope this. intent-dc measured that `test all` already runs every declared option and that `fullcycle` does not.

## Measured

- `_fullcycle_phases` prints exactly `clean rust`, `build all` and `test rust` (read by vc at HEAD). The dry run walks the same function, and tests/unit/fullcycle.bats asserts the three phases and their order.
- `test all` runs every declared, active test option not marked `in_all: false` (lib/resolve's run_all), and it runs with a single option: hv's own `bin/devbin test all` on devbin today reported "1 of 1 test options ran". docs/configuration.md says `all` is synthesised for a command "with more than one option", which reads narrower than that behaviour; whoever builds this should check that sentence.
- Intent's `test` declares `shell` and `rust` today (read from its config), so the fix below also brings Intent's shell tests into its full cycle.

## The shape of a fix (vc's recommendation; hv's to route)

- **A, recommended: the test phase is `test all`.** One definition of "the tests" shared by `test all` and `fullcycle`, which is what the relayed ruling asks of both. No new key: a project keeps an option out of both with the existing `in_all: false`, which `all` reports as skipped. It mirrors the `build all` phase beside it.
- B: a per-project list, eg `commands.fullcycle.tests`, defaulting to `rust`. That is a second place deciding which tests count, which A avoids.
- Either way the phase list stays defined once, in `_fullcycle_phases`, and fullcycle's messages that name `test rust` (the STOPPING line and the build-passed line) follow it.
- lib/cmd/fullcycle is vendored, so the change goes in the next sweep's pre-notice.

## Arms a fix needs

- fullcycle runs a second declared test option in its test phase, after `build all`, and its dry run lists it.
- An option marked `in_all: false` is skipped by fullcycle and reported as skipped.
- A project that declares only `rust` runs exactly what `test rust` runs today.
- A failure in the second option stops the cycle naming that option, with the build-passed line fullcycle already prints.

## From the Intent estate (intent-vc, 2026-09-17)

- Shape A is the one Intent would choose too: one definition of "the tests" for both commands, `in_all: false` as the override, and no new key.
- At Intent's HEAD, bin/.devbin/config.yaml declares `shell` (the BATS suite, through tests/run_tests.sh) and `rust`, neither marked `in_all: false`, and intent-dc's banked `toolchain` option joins them. Under A, Intent's full cycle gains the shell suite and, once it lands, the toolchain pass. Whether the shell suite belongs in a full cycle is hv's call, and `in_all: false` already expresses it.
- The Intent estate treats the vendored lib as devbin's: nothing there will patch lib/cmd/fullcycle locally in the meantime.

## Routing (hv, 2026-09-17)

- **vc builds now, ahead of ST0007 WP-03, and dc reviews**, ruled by hv in vc's session on vc's proposal, which named shape A, the one the Intent estate chose too: the test phase is `test all`, with `in_all: false` as the override. It goes first because the Intent estate waits on it.
- lib/cmd/fullcycle is vendored, so the change reaches Intent only through a fleet sweep, which is hv's go.

## Measured across the fleet (vc, 2026-09-17)

Read-only, in the same pass as 0082's census, at devbin `d6cb655`, 14:50Z: devbin's own resolver (`command_options`, `option_active`, `has_project_handler` from `lib/resolve`) over each of the 30 installs' configs. **`fullcycle` is offered in 6 of them**, the installs declaring `rust`. What the test phase runs in each, today and under `test all`:

| Install             | Today: `test rust`    | Under `test all`                                                            |
| ------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Conflab             | `rust`                | `rust`, `swift`, `mix`, `credo`                                             |
| Intent              | `rust`                | `shell`, `rust`, `toolchain`                                                |
| Laksa               | `rust`                | `mix`, `credo`, `rust`; `integration` and `local` skipped (`in_all: false`) |
| Lamplight           | its `test.d/rust` leg | its handler's `all`: rust, lua, credo, then mix                             |
| Utilz               | `rust`                | `rust`, `shell`                                                             |
| `_Archive/Intentv2` | `rust`                | `shell`, `rust`                                                             |

- **Lamplight is the one shape `in_all: false` cannot reach.** Its `test` is a handler that declares no options, so the cycle hands it `all` and its `test_all` runs all four legs, the ExUnit leg included. Only the handler can keep a leg out, and standing directive 4 makes `test all` at Lamplight hv-run.
- **Conflab's cycle gains its swift, mix and credo suites, and Laksa's its mix and credo suites.** Utilz's gains `test shell`, whose `run:` is the one value in 0082's census that relies on globbing.
- For the next sweep's pre-notice (vc's todo 51): the change reaches these installs only through a sweep, which is hv's go.

## Fixed 2026-09-17 -- fullcycle's test phase is `test all`, so `in_all: false` keeps a test option out of a full cycle as it does out of `test all` (vc), reviewed by dc

**Commits:**
- `6a48024`: the fix.
- `63ee125`: dc's review, two lows folded:
  - README.md carried a third copy of the "more than one option" sentence. It now says "at least one", and the 0.1.2 note names it.
  - Arm 46 now holds the cycle's `rc=1`. Its failing option exits 3, so the rc can only be `all`'s verdict. dc's D3, run_all's failure rc set to 7, had stayed green in every arm.

**What changed.**
- `_fullcycle_phases` runs `test all` where it ran `test rust`, so `fullcycle` and `test all` run the same tests.
- The refusal for a project with no build command lists the rest of the cycle, read from `_fullcycle_phases` less its build. It used to name `test rust` in a literal sentence.
- README.md, docs/configuration.md and docs/authoring-commands.md say `all` is synthesised for any command with at least one option. configuration.md adds that `in_all: false` keeps a test option out of a full cycle.
- RELEASES/0.1.2.md carries a Changed entry.

**Behaviour changes, for the sweep pre-notice:**
- Where `all` runs a project's options, the test phase's rc is `all`'s: 1 on any failure. `test rust` used to pass cargo's own code through. A handler that receives `all` still returns its own.
- A `test` handler that declares no options receives `all` from the cycle, where it received `rust`.
- A test phase whose every option is `in_all: false` refuses a verdict ("executed nothing"), so the cycle stops red.

**The first arm is narrowed, not met as written.** The dry run lists `bin/devbin test all`, the command the phase runs, and not the options `all` will run. There are three reasons, and dc's review confirmed the reading:
- `build all` beside it is not expanded either.
- Nothing but run_all reads `in_all`, so a member list would copy its filter into fullcycle.
- A handler that declares no options has no members in config to list.

**Arms, tests/unit/fullcycle.bats (49, was 42).**
- Renamed to `test all`: 3, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14 and 34.
- 43: a second declared option runs after the build, and `all` reports that all test options passed.
- 44: an `in_all: false` option is kept out, checked first, and reported skipped.
- 45: a project that declares only `rust` runs exactly what `test rust` runs, with cargo's argv and cwd compared.
- 46: a failing second option stops the cycle `rc=1` naming it, with the build-passed line. The log order shows `all` going on past the breach.
- 47: a test phase whose every option is excluded is red.
- 48: a handler with no declared options receives `all`.
- 49: the refusal reads `_fullcycle_phases`.

**Verified.**
- Red-first on the parent's lib: 11 of 47 arms red, and 48 red. Arm 45 is green there by design and dies under mutant M2.
- vc's 11 mutants were killed at their arms. dc rebuilt all 11 from the packet and killed them, with D1, D2 and D4 of dc's own.
- D3 survived until the fold. With it, arm 46 fails at its phase line under D3 (rc=7) and under a pass-through of the option's own rc (rc=3). D3 over the arm as it was stays 49/49 green.
- The full suite at 6a48024: 1..1335, 1335 ok, the 3 standing skips.
- critic-shell on the draft: 0 critical, 0 warning, and 4 recommendations, folded before the commit.

**Fleet effect** (measured above). The change reaches the six installs that offer `fullcycle` only through a sweep, which is hv's go. Lamplight's `cmd/build` keeps `all` as an alias for its `cli` build alone "for `dvb fullcycle`", and its `test_all` runs rust, lua, credo and mix (read by dc, and by vc). So the cycle Lamplight runs today is clean, the cli build and its rust leg, which standing directive 4 does not reach. Once swept, that cycle runs the ExUnit leg and becomes hv-run there. No config lever reaches a handler, and narrowing its `all` would reverse hv's 2026-08-09 ruling, so the choice is hv's; vc surfaced it.
